description: Macquarie University has been teaching actuarial studies since 1968. It is the first actuarial studies program in the English speaking world, and is the longest running program of its type in Australia. One-third to one-half of qualified actuaries in Australia are Macquarie graduates. Actuaries analyse and manage the financial consequences of risky events. These risks include risk of death or sickness, risk of natural hazards (cyclone, earthquake, bushfire), and financial risks (shares, bonds, exchange rates). Actuaries analyse and manage the risks of financial contracts, insurance and retirement funds. They also help manage and control financial institutions. Actuaries relate numbers to real life. In this actuarial studies degree you’ll learn to conduct mathematical, statistical, economic and financial analysis to a range of practical problems faced in long-term financial planning and management. Very strong industry links exist through capstone and professional subjects including the actuarial control cycle. Key features: Accredited by the Actuaries Institute, giving you a head start in your professional exams. Provides a comprehensive understanding in not only actuarial studies but also in economics, accounting, mathematics, statistics and finance. In your final year, your advanced skills will allow you to undertake actuarial projects on insurance liability and risk. Taught by the largest actuarial department in Australia, students will learn from highly experienced lecturers and members of the Actuaries Institute. Many Macquarie actuarial graduates hold senior positions in the financial services industry.

description: The Bachelor of Speech and Hearing Sciences equips students with a comprehensive and evidence-based understanding of linguistics – the scientific study of human communication –, with a focus on speech, hearing, and language sciences. Students will explore how language is structured, produced, perceived, and understood, with a strong focus on the diversity of human communication across the lifespan and across cultures. description: The Overview and Aims of the course have been defined in terms of a Vision statement and associated Mission and Design statements, as provided below. Vision To create a medical course which provides a truly transnational quality assured medical education experience for local and international students. While embedded in learning within the Australian health care context, a strong emphasis on the comparison of health care systems and on emerging technologies in medical practice will ensure that our students master the cultural awareness and communication skills required for positive patient-centred care in any setting. Macquarie University graduates will be doctors who capably practice quality medicine in diverse local and global communities, and effectively connect with patients and inter-professional teams across cultures. Mission The primary mission of the Medical course is to graduate doctors with the scientific, clinical, social and professional capabilities that will serve as the basis for medical practice across the world. By collaborating with domestic and international partners who share similar value sets, we will provide an outstanding clinical and educational experience locally and globally. Our primary mission will be realised through our commitment to: Comparative and reflective approach to learning. We will use a comparative approach to the varied clinical, cultural and health system experiences of the course's diverse group of students. By encouraging reflection on these experiences, we will foster the achievement of an international perspective and a global capability set for our graduates. Patient-centred Care. We will graduate doctors who will make the quality of the care of patients their first concern, ensuring health care systems work well for their patients, and applying their knowledge and skills in a practical, professional and ethical manner. They will be practitioners focusing on quality, safety, efficiency, patient advocacy, and team-based care. Innovation. We will develop a course that focuses on the role of health systems in the provision of quality care, and on the emerging technologies that will be required for medical practice into the future. Cultural competence. We will prepare doctors who are aware of the impact of their own culture and values on their medical practice, and have knowledge of, respect for and sensitivity towards the cultural needs of diverse populations, including Indigenous people. The development of cultural competence will be embedded in the education process of the course. Research, and Science-based Practice. We will prepare graduates with research skills who understand how knowledge is discovered and applied, and who will lead the improvement of health and medical care through scholarship and research-informed practice. Design This course has been designed to develop the following 4 graduate capabilities, each with two aspects, which underpin the course learning outcomes: Capability 1 Scientist and Scholar : Graduates will be applied medical scientists and scholars with advanced knowledge and skills to deliver and advance science- and evidence-based medicine. Capability 2 Clinical Practitioner: Graduates will be effective communicators and highly skilled, competent doctors delivering safe, patient-centred healthcare. Capability 3 Engaged Global Citizen: Graduates will be socially and culturally responsive practitioners with awareness of local and global public health issues, and who are ready to operate effectively in a range of health systems. Capability 4 Professional: Graduates will be ethical and reflective medical practitioners ready to lead and work collaboratively within teams.

description: Clinical trials are a fundamental part of medical research, advancing science and promoting human health. They serve to evaluate the effect of new interventions, medications, and devices on health outcomes and underpin regulatory approvals around the world for current therapies supporting care of patients with all manner of diseases and conditions. The MTPConnect report into Australia’s Clinical Trials Sector (MTPConnect, 2021, Australia’s Clinical Trials Sector, mtpconnect.org.au) which was commissioned by the Australian Government, identified that the number of clinical trials being conducted is increasing by 6.6% per year globally. Currently, the majority of education of professionals who support clinical trials occurs informally in the workplace or through short courses. There is a critical need for establishing accredited qualifications and training programs in the longer-term. The MTPConnect report highlighted a critical shortage of skilled staff in this sector in Australia and identified ‘growing the clinical trials workforce and developing its capabilities’ as a key priority for the continued growth of trials in Australia. Given the predicted critical workforce shortage of skilled professionals, the Graduate Certificate of Clinical Trials Operations was developed and co-designed with industry experts to provide formal Clinical Trial operations and management relevant training. This course is intended for professionals seeking to work in clinical trials or professionals in the industry seeking to further develop their skills with a formal qualification and has been designed to develop the following 4 graduate capabilities: Capability 1. Scientist and Scholar : Graduates will be applied scientists and research-informed scholars with advanced knowledge and skills to deliver science- and evidence-based practice in clinical trials conduct and management. Capability 2. Clinical Trial Practitioner: Graduates will be effective communicators and highly skilled, competent professionals delivering and managing safe, patient-centred clinical trials and produce credible data. Capability 3. Engaged Global Citizen: Graduates will be socially and culturally responsive with awareness of local and global issues associated with clinical trials. Capability 4. Professional: Graduates will be ethical and reflective professionals ready to lead and work collaboratively within teams. This course promotes the highest ethical standards and is compliant with current Australian and International regulations. The curriculum has been mapped to internationally recognised Core Competency Frameworks for Clinical Research Professionals. Graduates will be well prepared for roles such as Clinical Trial Coordinators, Clinical Research Associates and Monitors and Ethics Committee Coordinators.

description: The Graduate Certificate of Financial Integrity Law offers a rigorous academic exploration of critical aspects of financial crime mitigation and regulatory compliance. Delivered through a structured curriculum, this certificate program provides participants with in-depth insights into the multifaceted dimensions of financial crimes and compliance. Participants will explore the inner workings of financial systems, analysing the mechanisms employed in the prevention and detection of various types of financial crimes. Central to the course is the examination of intergovernmental organisations like the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and regulatory bodies such as the Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre (AUSTRAC), focusing on their roles in mitigating illicit financing activities. Through a series of comprehensive units, participants will investigate the complexities surrounding international sanctions regimes, Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Counter-Terrorist Financing (CTF), and Counter-Proliferation Financing (CPF). Furthermore, participants will gain an understanding of the legal underpinnings of corporate governance and the evolving landscape of Cyber Crime or Forensic Accounting. Participants will engage in scholarly discourse, case analyses, and practical applications to deepen their understanding of theoretical concepts and real-world implications. The certificate program offers a flexible face-to-face and online learning environment, enabling participants to access course materials, lectures, and discussions at their convenience.

description: Lymphoedema is a chronic inflammatory condition which is the result of a functional overload of the lymphatic system whereby the lymph volume exceeds lymphatic transport capacity. Lymphoedema is a poorly understood and under-researched condition which can significantly impact physical and psychological function, reduce quality of life and result in substantial cost burdens to both patients and the healthcare system. Lymphoedema has increasing prevalence as a result of people surviving cancers and living longer lives. This course is for health professionals seeking to provide evidence-based care to people at risk of, or living with, lymphoedema and chronic oedemas. The units are also mapped to the Australasian Lymphology Association (ALA) Competency Standards, which is the peak body in Australia, and includes all learning needed to be accredited as a Lymphoedema Therapist in Australia relative to the health professional's scope of practice. Capability 2. Clinical Practitioner: Graduates will be effective communicators and highly skilled, competent clinicians delivering safe, patient-centred lymphoedema and chronic oedema healthcare. Capability 3. Engaged Global Citizen: Graduates will be socially and culturally responsive practitioners with awareness of local and global public health issues associated with lymphoedema and chronic oedemas, and who are ready to operate effectively in a range of health systems. Capability 4. Professional: Graduates will be ethical and reflective clinicians ready to lead and work collaboratively within teams. This course promotes the highest ethical standards and is compliant with current Australian and International regulations. Graduates will be well prepared to work in both the public and private sectors working with people at risk of or living with lymphoedema and chronic oedemas.

description: The Master of Clinical Audiology (MClinAudiology) is a two year postgraduate course located within the Department of Linguistics at Macquarie University. It is a unique offering in NSW with only six other professionally accredited programs existing in Australia (Victoria, Queensland, South Australia, Western Australia and the Northern Territory). Our location, within the Australian Hearing Hub offers our students the unique ability to interact with a wide variety of hearing researchers (Cochlear and National Acoustics Laboratories), hearing care service providers like the Next Sense, Shepherd Centre and other allied health partners (such as speech pathologists, teachers of the Deaf, and early intervention specialists). The Macquarie University Master of Clinical Audiology course aims to provide our students with the skills, knowledge and training they need to practice as a qualified clinical audiologist. The course prepares students for the assessment, rehabilitation, and habilitation of populations with hearing impairment, as well as training in research studies' design. Our Macquarie University audiology graduates will be competent practitioners with strong scholarly, social, and professional abilities and highly employable, capable of engaging across disciplines, with diverse local and global communities. The Master of Clinical Audiology program is two years in duration. The first-year focusses on diagnostic and knowledge-based and skill-based outcomes, while the second-year centres on clinical management of clients, their families, and clinical practice more broadly, including understanding the hearing healthcare system and how it fits within the healthcare system more broadly. The structure is designed so that it systematically segues to ensure progression and development of competencies throughout the two years. As such, the degree has been designed to develop the following four graduate capabilities: Capability 1 Scientist and Scholar : Graduates will be clinical hearing scientists and research-informed scholars with a broad range of knowledge and skills relevant to the field of audiology. Capability 2 Practitione r : Graduates will be effective communicators and highly skilled, technically competent clinical audiologists able to deliver safe and effective care. Capability 3 Citizen : Graduates will be inclusive, culturally respectful and ethical practitioners, able to advocate for hearing health locally and globally. Capability 4 Professional : Graduates will be ethical and reflective clinical audiologists able to work collaboratively within teams, and a range of organisations, and direct their lifelong learning.

description: The Master of Organisational Psychology course includes units that integrate theory with psychological practice, together with 1,000 hours of supervised placement, and a research project. Students completing this course typically work as organisational psychologists in consultancy firms, large companies, or government departments in areas such as personnel selection, human resource management, training, organisational development, workplace and career counselling, user experience testing, and/or occupational health and safety. The course aims are to develop graduates who can: Satisfy professional standards in psychology; Communicate effectively, personally and digitally, with a wide range of clients and professionals; Integrate psychological theories and evidence with practical problem-solving in the context of organisational psychology; Implement and interpret psychological assessments of individuals and groups; Diagnose impediments to psychological health and well-being in the workplace; Select, design, implement, and evaluate evidence-based interventions in the context of organisational psychology; Collaborate with, or refer to, other professionals when work is outside their professional capabilities; Demonstrate cultural sensitivity and a capacity to develop and implement interventions that account for diversity; Develop an ongoing professional capability through self-reflective, ethical practice; and Develop an ongoing professional capability by undertaking applied research. Therefore, the degree has been specifically designed to develop the following four graduate capabilities: Capability 1. Scientist and Scholar : Graduates will be research-informed applied psychologists, equipped with advanced knowledge and skills in best-practice principles and evidence-based techniques relevant to the practice of organisational psychology. Capability 2. Psychologist Practitioner : Graduates will be effective multi-modal communicators and highly skilled, competent psychologists, able to deliver safe, client-centered psychological services across a broad range of organisational psychological practice. Capability 3. Engaged Global Citizen : Graduates will be socially and culturally responsive psychologists with awareness of local and global issues associated with the practice of organisational psychology and who are ready to operate effectively in a range of community, government, health and organisational systems. Capability 4. Professional : Graduates will be ethical and reflective psychologists ready to lead and work collaboratively within organisational teams.

description: The 1-year Master of Professional Psychology course includes coursework units that combine professional psychology theory and practice, together with a minimum of 300 hours of supervised placement activity. Placements are supervised in-field by appropriately trained Psychologists who are also Psychology Board of Australia (PsyBA) approved supervisors. Opportunities for placements and potential employment following include, but not not limited to, working in: schools (public and private); hospitals and clinics; not-for-profit community services; government departments and agencies; drug and alcohol counselling; workplace rehabilitation, and assessment and report-writing roles. Students completing this course will have acquired the knowledge and skills for 5th-year training in professional psychology, required to undertake a PsyBA approved 6th-year internship and, in turn, the National Psychology Exam (NPE), as part of the 5+1 internship pathway to registration as a Psychologist. The course structure provides a progression from core knowledge and skills to more specialised training, consistent with key professional practice goals and standards, and allowing for coursework to be integrated with mandatory placement requirements. The course aims to produce graduates who: Meet the core graduate competencies for Level 3 Professional Psychology Programs, as per the standards outlined by the Australian Psychology Accreditation Council (APAC), in preparation for their 6th-year internship as a Provisional Psychologist. Integrate theory and evidence-based practice to deliver safe quality client care and service as a Psychologist. Reflect and evaluate on their own practice, recognise limitations and refer as appropriate to other colleagues. Engage diverse clients in a broad range of services across different professional practice settings. Demonstrate commitment to the scientist-practitioner model evidenced by their informed choice of psychological assessments, therapies, intervention design and evaluation of practice. Communicate effectively and work collaboratively with clients, fellow health professionals, and the wider community. Think independently as evidenced by their ability to analyse and synthesise relevant information and readily apply their knowledge and skills to new environments and situations. Continually evaluate their practice and abilities, to take action as necessary and commit to life-long learning in professional psychology. Show leadership and advocacy capabilities on behalf of their clients and the profession. As such, the degree has been specifically designed to develop the following four graduate capabilities: Capability 1. Scientist and Scholar: Graduates will be research-informed and applied provisional psychologists, equipped with advanced knowledge and skills in best-practice principles and evidence-based techniques relevant to the practice of psychology. Capability 2. Psychologist Practitioner: Graduates will be effective multi-modal communicators and highly skilled, competent provisional psychologists, able to deliver safe, client-centered psychological services across a broad range of psychological practice. Capability 3. Engaged Global Citizen: Graduates will be socially and culturally responsive provisional psychologists with awareness of local and global issues associated with the practice of psychology and who are ready to operate effectively in a range of community, government, health and organisational systems. Capability 4. Professional: Graduates will be ethical and reflective provisional psychologists ready to lead and work collaboratively within teams.

description: The Master of Strategy and Security equips current and future leaders to address the most pressing security challenges confronting their nation or business. Graduates will be able to formulate strategies that anticipate, adapt, and respond to security threats, challenges, and risks. This interdisciplinary postgraduate degree brings together world-class academics and top professionals from Government and industry to create an exciting and dynamic learning environment. Students will be challenged to think deeply on pressing risks and threats – ranging from war, coercion, foreign influence, terrorism, crime, biosecurity threats, and cyber-attacks – and how governments, societies, and businesses from across the Indo-Pacific region can respond to ensure they remain secure and prosperous. The degree combines elements of classroom study with more dynamic simulations, wargaming, and scenario-based learning. The Master of Strategy and Security is focused on preparing the next generation of analysts, practitioners, officials, and industry leaders with the skills and knowledge they need to keep their nation or organisation safe. Students can specialise in one of three areas: (a) Defence and Strategy, (b) Cyber Intelligence, or (c) Counter Terrorism.

description: The Master of Sustainable Development serves the needs for professional roles in sustainability, in business, industry, the public sector, international organisations, non-government organisations, research think tanks, academia and consultancies. CONTEXT Sustainable development is an internationally embraced imperative oriented to meeting the needs of a growing population for social and economic development while addressing social justice, and ensuring the integrity of the planetary systems to support all life now and for the future. There are Global Goals for Sustainable Development which provide a focus for policy, strategy and action by all countries and organisations. In 2018 Australia made its first report on the national and international actions undertaken for the Sustainable Development Goals in 2018. While Australia provides good case material for learning with good progress on many of the social development goals there are many challenges for the nation such as the rise of inequality and disadvantage, climate change, regional development in Australia, sustainable cities, and the continuing loss of biodiversity. DISTINCTIVE FEATURES OF THE MACQUARIE PROGRAM The Master of Sustainable Development has a strong focus on the importance of the quality of the environmental systems and ecological economics to support present and future social development. The core of the degree has a focus on how to effect changes towards sustainable development and to work with stakeholders with diverse perspectives and values and provides students with an option to hone skills to work with business and organisations on bringing about change for sustainability. The degree includes an Australian and international outlook through case studies, and exposes students to field work, practical examples of sustainability in Australia, and interaction with sustainability practitioners and a work practice experience as a consultant. The degree provides options for students to broaden or deepen capabilities in a diverse range of disciplinary options from the environment, economics, law, social science, business and policy. The degree assists those who wish to integrate more sustainable thinking and innovation into their existing profession or who wish to change professions to be in a more ethically oriented field.

In keeping with Macquarie University's vision to promote research-intensive learning and teaching, critical, analytical and integrative thinking skills are incorporated into all units in this degree. Students apply their understandings, skills and specialist early childhood knowledge through engagement with children across the birth to five years range in a variety of early childhood environments.
